title: Mode mixing, avoided crossings, damping, and drag
question: Do the implemented lower-order vector and carrier operators reproduce exact crossings, mixed-mode repulsion, cleaning decay, electric damping, and relaxation-time-dependent counterflow decay without violating conservation or entropy production?
prediction: The uncoupled vector mass sweep has one exact crossing while nonzero mixing opens one avoided crossing with 50 percent field mixing; cleaning and electric decay match their analytic matrix exponents within 1e-10; and production carrier drag follows exp(-dt/tau), strengthens monotonically as tau decreases, conserves energy and momentum, and produces nonnegative entropy.
falsifier: Failure to resolve the crossing controls, damping error above tolerance, nonmonotone drag, negative heat or entropy, or a drag-induced energy or momentum change falsifies the lower-order map.
controls: The zero-mixing mass sweep is the exact-crossing control for the nonzero-mixing avoided crossing.
Vector eigenmass gaps and field participation are computed from the production Gauss matrix.
Cleaning damping is measured from the actual Fourier RHS generator and compared to its quadratic roots.
Electric damping initializes each analytic damping-matrix eigenvector independently.
The gamma_B=0 common electric mode is retained as an undamped zero-heat control.
Carrier drag is applied through the production implicit collision map, not a stand-alone exponential assignment.
Pre-drag conserved energy and momentum arrays are immutable comparison controls.
seed_rationale: All parameter sweeps, eigenmodes, and homogeneous production states are deterministic.
